gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-inika: Inika reads like a classic serif, with gaps you can see through. Happy Monkey sits above it with bold, ruler-straight strokes, so a long page of text feels lively without turning loud.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-kay-pho-du: Chunky, bold, a bit cheeky. Happy Monkey draws every line the same width, and Kay Pho Du follows with text serif counters that breathe like a hollow reed cut open.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-labrada: Labrada reads with wide openings on small letters, dignified and bookish. Happy Monkey's bowls are drawn at stem thickness, so the two feel like a toy box set beside a library shelf.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-montaga: Montaga's pen-lifted curves leave each loop unfinished, giving the classic serif an editorial, bookish air. Over a long passage that makes for a thoughtful, stitched-thread rhythm under Happy Monkey.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-new-tegomin: Bent-tubing letters, all one gauge, give Happy Monkey its bold, distinctive look. And New Tegomin, a classic serif with a c like a wide-open ring, settles the page into something traditional and dignified.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-podkova: Happy Monkey draws its joins as thick as its strokes, so it grabs attention fast. But Podkova, a classic serif with a broad, welcoming c, is the one built to carry the bookish, traditional text.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-rhodium-libre: Pipe-cleaner letters, bold and bendy. Rhodium Libre follows as a classic serif whose brush ends lift away before each curve closes, so a long passage keeps an editorial, traditional feel beneath Happy Monkey.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-rokkitt: Heavy diagonals, full-strength verticals, zero shyness. Happy Monkey brings the shout, and Rokkitt, a serif with a c as open as a bent paperclip, answers it with bookish, traditional manners.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-sanchez: Happy Monkey has round bowls whose walls never swell. Its strongest quality is the contrast with Sanchez, a bookish, dignified text serif with a c opened like a pair of calipers.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-solway: Solway is an authoritative text serif with sign-painter's-stencil flatness and a generous entry into the e's eye. Under Happy Monkey, a longer passage feels bookish and steady.
